text:
Alex H: heads up — BrightBooks escalated: after yesterday's model push some vendor names in their invoice parser are coming back as `UNKNOWN`. They say this started right after the rollout. Internal evals for the same task still show >95% pass so this looks like an eval vs. customer input mismatch. attaching the customer prompt they pasted into the API (redacted):

Alex H: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.4-optim","input":"Parse vendor name:

Vendor: Acme Corp
Invoice: 2024-09-30
---
Please output vendor only."}'
```

Priya S: can you paste the exact raw bytes / request_id for the failing call?

Alex H: request_id=req_0a9f3b2c, model=redwood-1.4-optim, customer provided the vendor string as part of a larger cell paste. here's the exact snippet they pasted (you won't see it in the UI):

Alex H: `Vendor:\u200b Acme Corp`  <-- note there is an invisible char between `:` and `A` (zero-width space U+200B)

Kevin L: interesting. I tried reproducing locally by inserting a U+200B and I get different tokenization / truncation behavior. internal evals strip/control for invisible chars which explains the discrepancy. repro steps:

Kevin L: ```python
raw = 'Vendor:\u200b Acme Corp'
print(list(raw.encode('utf-8')))  # shows b'... e2 80 8b ...'
# quick detect strip
clean = raw.replace('\u200b','')
```

Kevin L: when the model sees the zero-width char it ends up splitting tokens differently and some vendor tokens get interpreted as out-of-vocab for our quantized token mapping, leading to fallback label `UNKNOWN` in the downstream parser.

Alex H: what was the rollout % for 1.4-optim? did we change any default normalizers?

Deploy Bot: canary: redwood-1.4-optim rolled to 25% at 1951232000; promoted to 100% at 1951234000. No normalization flags were toggled in the rollout config.

Maria R: customer said they copied names from Google Sheets / Excel which can inject invisible chars (thin spaces / ZWSP). I told them a workaround (manually delete and retype) but we need an RCA + fix.

Kevin L: immediate mitigation options:
- Add server-side input normalization that removes common invisible/formatting chars (U+200B, U+200C, BOM) before tokenization. low-risk patch.
- In SDK/console add a checkbox "Normalize whitespace and invisible chars" for pastes.
- Add tests to the eval harness that include raw customer paste cases so we don't regress silently.

Kevin L: quick patch PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4387 (adds strip_zwsp pre-tokenize). Deployable as hotfix to canary.

Alex H: can we get patch to canary now? if it fixes BrightBooks we can push to prod and update them.

Deploy Bot: patch PR referenced; CI green. Hotfix canary deploy scheduled at 1951237900.

CS Bot: updated ticket TCK-9876 with root-cause notes and workaround (SDK snippet to .replace('\u200b','')). Customer notified and asked for sample script.

Priya S: follow-ups: add a column of raw customer inputs to our regression eval suite (two examples from BrightBooks), and add a telemetry flag to log when non-printing unicode is present so we can monitor prevalence.

Maria R: I'll coordinate the customer comms + escalate for an SLA credit if they request one.

Kevin L: long-term: tighten tokenization mapping for quantized models to avoid OOV for single invisible-char shifts, and expand eval corpora to include paste-induced artifacts.

Alex H: great — thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket once canary hotfix completes. :thumbsup:
